title: Over-Refusal Asymmetry: Do Safety Improvements Always Increase Over-Refusal Proportionally?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: the safety vs. over-refusal Pareto frontier is critical for deployment. Identifying which intervention achieves best safety-per-unit-over-refusal directly informs deployment-time intervention choices.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires applying three distinct safety interventions (SFT, DPO, activation steering) to a model and evaluating each on two benchmarks. Multiple training procedures and activation steering implementation demand advanced ML skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three separate interventions each requiring different tooling, plus evaluation on two benchmarks per intervention. This is effectively three experiments combined, well beyond a 30-hour scope.

novelty.reasoning: OR-Bench (ICML 2025) provides the first large-scale over-refusal benchmark with 80,000 prompts. The 'Alignment Tax' (arXiv:2603.00047, 2026) formalizes the alignment-capability tradeoff as an elliptic Pareto frontier. ACTOR (2025) reduces over-refusals while maintaining safety. Sorry-Bench (ICLR 2025) evaluates safety-helpfulness tradeoffs. However, the specific comparison of safety-per-unit-over-refusal across three distinct intervention types (SFT, DPO, activation steering) on a single model is not directly available. The Pareto frontier framing exists but the specific multi-intervention comparison adds some value.
